 Judgment

The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.73 of 2013 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Palakkad is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 19.05.2012.
The petitioner was a two year old child at the time of the accident.

According to the petitioner, on 19.05.2012 at about 04.30 p.m., while the minor child was riding pillion on a motorcycle, a lorry bearing registration No.KL-08-L-4555 driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on the motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, the child fell down and his right leg above knee was amputated.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.54,55,000/, limited to Rs.35,00,000/-.

4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of MACA NO. 2345 OF 2017 2025:KER:32974 the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A10.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,02,700/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri.Jacob Sebastian, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.K.J.Saji Isaac, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.

sentences.text: The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.3,000/-.
According to him, the notional income of the petitioner is to be fixed at least as that of a coolie during the relevant year.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
(1) Crush injury on the right leg (2) Open fracture on the right leg (3) Amputation of right leg above knee (4) Laceration and abrasion all over the body 12.
As per Exhibit A3 disability certificate issued by the District Hospital, Palakkad his permanent physical disability was assessed as 50%.
Before the Tribunal, no disability certificate was produced.
However, the Tribunal has fixed his disability at 6%.
As per Annexure - A2, the petitioner has produced a disability certificate issued by District Hospital, Palakkad, in which his permanent physical disability was assessed as 50%.

13. However relying upon Sl.No.18 of part II schedule I of the Employees Compensation Act, the learned counsel would argue that in case of amputation below hip with stump exceeding 12.70 cms.
in length measured from tip of great trenchanter but not beyond middle thigh, the percentage of loss of earning capacity will come to 70% and as such the functional disability in this case is to be taken as 70%.

entities.text: Sl.No.18 of part II schedule I
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: Since as per part II schedule I of the Employees Compensation Act amputation of leg above knee amounts to 70% of loss of earning capacity, the functional disability of the petitioner is fixed at 70%.
14. The compensation payable on the basis of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme court in Master Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, MACA NO. 2345 OF 2017 2025:KER:32974 National Insurance Co.Ltd.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, MACA NO. 2345 OF 2017 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And Another, (2014)SCC 396 to a child suffering from 60-90% disability is only Rs.500000/-.
In the facts of this, case awarding just Rs.500000/- to the petitioner who suffered 70% functional disability due to amputation of his right leg above knee will not be just and reasonable.
Even the above decision provides for a different treatment in exceptional cases and this is such an exceptional one.

15. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2012 will come to Rs.8,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for fixing the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.8,500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
As argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner, because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner at the age of 2 lost his right leg above the knee.

Therefore, for the purpose of awarding just and reasonable compensation on the head loss of disability, his notional income is fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.8,500/-.
16.

Since, on the date of accident the petitioner was a child aged 2 years, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.

3 Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC MACA NO. 2345 OF 2017 2025:KER:32974 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.14,99,400/-.
17. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.22,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.15,000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.3,000/- was awarded.
Towards bystander expenses, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.2,700/-.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
18. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 30 days and his functional disability is 70%.
Because of the injuries sustained in the accident, his right leg above knee was amputated.

Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life', 'extra nourishment' and 'bystander expenses' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-, Rs.1,50,000/-, Rs.20,000/- and Rs.6,000/- (Rs.200/- x 30 months) respectively.
17. The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expense.
No compensation was awarded towards cost of prosthesis or its maintenance.

The learned counsel has produced Annexure - A9 certificate issued from Ottobock, stating that since the petitioner was aged 2 year old at the time of the accident at least 15 to 20 times the prosthesis will have to be changed.
The average expense MACA NO. 2345 OF 2017 2025:KER:32974 of prosthesis will vary from Rs.1,00,000/- to Rs.6,00,000/-.
Annexure - A1 produced by the petitioner shows that he has already spent a sum of Rs.1,70,480/- till 09.11.2016 towards the cost of prosthesis.

19. In the decision in Vivek G. v. National Insurance Company Ltd. [2023 KHC 2941], in case of a 12 year old child whose right leg was to be amputated in an accident in the year 2011, the Hon'ble Apex Court has awarded a total sum of Rs.26,00,000/- including Rs.20,00,000/- being the cost of 4 prosthesis and a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- towards the cost of its maintenance.

entities.text: Vivek G. v. National Insurance Company Ltd. [2023 KHC 2941]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, since the victim was a 2 year old child, he needs frequent change of prosthesis, till he grows into an adult.
He will also require considerable amount for the maintenance of the prosthesis.
Therefore, I hold that towards the cost of prosthesis and its maintenance, he is entitled to get a compensation in tune with the decision in Vivek G. (supra).
Therefore, towards cost of prosthesis and its maintenance a sum of Rs.26,00,000/- is granted.
Out of which Rs.20,00,000/- will carry interest only from the date of this judgment.

20. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the right leg of the petitioner was amputated above knee, the same will adversely affect his marriage prospects and as such, he is entitled to get compensation for loss of marriage prospects.

Since there is merit in the above argument, a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded towards MACA NO.
2345 OF 2017 2025:KER:32974 loss of marriage prospects.
21.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
